## 1. The step

A step is the activation of one reference frame, or one declared active
frame configuration, on an exact subject (REFERENCE_FRAME §1, §11). Its
context is the projection of that activated frame to the actor; the corpus
or the workspace is never the context (P0; RF-002). Intake, admission,
applicability and activation are distinct relations inside the step even
when one invocation performs all of them.

When construction is delegated to a probabilistic or agentic worker, the
method governs the execution relation without prescribing the worker's
model, prompt, tools, internal search, process topology, repository layout
or orchestration runtime (P0; the work boundary of FOUNDATIONS §2). The
normative relation runs: accepted governing basis; bounded affected
relation set; selected computational relations; delegated execution and
decision authority; construction and self-review; independent live-surface
assessment where required; one of accept, local repair, re-enter or reject
(§3); the exact accepted checkpoint; the next already-authorised bounded
action (§5). Provenance:
[UP-020](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#agentic-construction-execution-stdo-up-020).

### Transitions

Construction moves work from a current state towards a destination
(P0, P2). The current state is the material state of the workspace and
its authoritative inputs, together with what is justifiably known about
that state, with the unknowns explicit. The work state of §5 records it:
the workspace, the governing basis, and the closed results and judgments
that still apply, with the residuals and the uncertainty over external
effects as the explicit unknowns. An actor's context is an account of the
current state, not the state itself
([§5](#the-workspace-and-an-actors-account)) (P3, P5).

The destination is defined by constraints: the selected outcome with its
acceptance conditions (Outcome U, [FOUNDATIONS §2](FOUNDATIONS.md#2-ontology))
and the governing obligations the work must keep. It names no single
state: its acceptance conditions admit several realised states. Its
owning authority defines it (P2, P6).

A transition is a bounded change from the current state to a next state,
carried out by one step. Where the work exceeds one activation's capacity,
the outer transformation towards the destination is refined into a series
of bounded transitions under §4 Refinement, each carried out by its own
step; work that fits one activation is a single transition. Each
transition binds the obligations it must preserve: the outer obligations
of the destination and of the governing relations it affects, as far as
they apply to it. A step's intake binds the current state, the
destination and the obligations: the governed outcome names the
destination, or the prerequisite towards it, that the step serves; the
exact subject and basis identify the current state it starts from; and
the affected relation set with its governing invariants holds the
obligations it preserves (Intake below; P0, P4a).
Transitions compose only as §4 Refinement permits.

Discovery. Construction, observation and evaluation change the current
state and what is known about it. A new observation may add obligations,
which join the known work, or invalidate a claim, which is re-established
or withdrawn before anything relies on it (§7). Discovery can enlarge the
known work while knowledge improves (P5, P4b).

Open work outside attention. An obligation outside a frame's current

## 1. Claims

A load-bearing claim names its exact subject, the property claimed, the
governing basis, the relation between witness and claim, the nearest weaker
property it excludes, and its falsifier, before a witness is selected.
Without these it is evidence discovery, not proof. Packaging, syntax,
compilation, presence, invocation or local behaviour never substitutes for a
semantic, authority-bearing, installed, release or end-to-end claim because
the weaker property is easier to measure (P6; conserves
[UP-001](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#proof-target-identity-and-adequacy-stdo-up-001)).

Where a claim about a construction concerns its recursive or repeated
work, it is one of the four kinds the construction relation keeps apart,
preservation, progress, termination and outcome satisfaction
([ACTIVATION §1](ACTIVATION.md#construction-relation)), and states which.
Its witness is an assertion whose predicate is the full obligation, a
necessary condition of it or part of a sufficient conjunction, and the
claim states which. Its expected result has assertion provenance and its
execution has execution provenance, as
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Assertions and observation](FOUNDATIONS.md#assertions-and-observation)
and [Parallel derivation and mutual assurance](FOUNDATIONS.md#parallel-derivation-and-mutual-assurance)
define them; a passing check of a necessary condition establishes that
condition and no more (P1, P6).

Boundary congruence. A checker, validator, harness, reviewer or other
assurance surface supporting promotion or closure binds the exact claimed
subject and its authoritative composition relation. Evidence over one file
or carrier proves only that boundary; it cannot establish a multi-file or
carrier-set claim. Cross-carrier satisfaction and conflict are decided at
the declared composite boundary (P3, P6). A claim of mechanical enforcement
names an executable or reproducible predicate and a witness reachable
through the declared ordinary assurance path; a planned or
specification-only harness is planned evidence, not observed verification,
and until both the predicate and such a witness are observed the claim
remains open or is explicitly downgraded to the planned property (P6;
conserves
[UP-022](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#assurance-boundary-congruence-and-method-qualification-stdo-up-022),
first two paragraphs).

A claim's quantifier, population and scope cannot exceed its evaluated
evidence. Generalising a local defect or observation needs a declared
inference relation, the relevant comparable population, explicit
counterexample treatment and governing evidence. Later counterevidence
invalidates every dependent verdict until the claim-evidence relation is
superseded, withdrawn or requalified (UP-022). The quantifier rule and the
boundary rule are false if assurance observes a weaker or different
subject, if per-carrier evidence closes an unevaluated composite claim, if
mechanical enforcement lacks its predicate or a reachable witness, if
planned evidence is reported as observed verification, if a verdict outruns
its evaluated population or declared inference relation, or if dependent
verdicts survive material counterevidence without requalification.

### Foundation to law: claims, evidence, assessment and acceptance

of [FOUNDATIONS §3 Foundation to law](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundation-to-law)),
decides when a claim is supported, how it is assessed and who accepts it.

about exact subjects are relied on for promotion, closure or release; (b)
the evidence available is finite, and may observe a weaker or different
subject, or another basis, than the one claimed; (c) a constructing actor
may be probabilistic or otherwise fallible; (d) each boundary at which a
claim is relied on has a decision owner. They are conditions of the work
this family governs, not commitments, and do not follow from finite
capacity alone.
P0's premise that a step's output is a candidate until evaluated is cited
by name. The standing of the consequences below is stated in
[FOUNDATIONS §3 Foundation to law](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundation-to-law).

Each consumer applies the rule and decides nothing the owning section does
not (P2, P6).

## 2. Separation

Three bases stay distinct (P6, P1): the semantic basis, the constitutional
and accepted-design relations that define what a claim means; the evidence
basis, the exact artifacts, events, logs, tests and observations used to
evaluate it; and the state projection, a current view derived from admitted
semantic and evidence bases. Semantic law defines what an evaluation means;
evidence supplies observations; the evaluator applies the declared
relation; decision authority disposes. One actor may lawfully perform
several; the record keeps them distinguishable. This section owns these
separations. [RF-007](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-007-semantic-evidence-and-verdict-separation)
binds them to a frame declaration and
[AC-018](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-018-structural-and-semantic-separation)
to an a_c model; each adds only its domain binding.

An evidence change can invalidate a verdict without any change of law.
Whether a given change does so is decided by the reuse rule of
[ACTIVATION §7](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse), and where it
does, the invalidation is mandatory and takes effect before reliance. A
projection change can invalidate a view without changing semantic truth;
when a derived view is stale is decided by
[ACTIVATION §2, Staleness of derived surfaces](ACTIVATION.md#staleness-of-derived-surfaces).
A semantic change requires lawful re-entry and invalidates affected
downstream acceptance. A broad digest may conservatively
invalidate a review; it does not prove that every semantic relation
changed (conserves
[UP-008](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/SPEC_METHOD.md#semantic-evidence-and-projection-separation-stdo-up-008),
[RF-007](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#rf-007-semantic-evidence-and-verdict-separation)).

## 1. Purpose and position

### Purpose

This profile exists for projects that want a stronger implementation
discipline than "write code that passes" (P2; rc.2 #1-purpose). Its bias is
toward low coupling, modular composition, immutable typed carriers, total
or nearly total semantic transforms and explicit effect boundaries. The
goal is not language ideology. The goals are to reduce ambiguity, reduce
entropy, eliminate avoidable technical debt, increase refactorability,
reduce hidden authority, hidden mutation and semantic drift in realisation
code, and preserve enough evidence that later reviewers can audit,
refactor and reconstruct why the realisation took its current shape (P2,
P6). The profile is therefore about realisation design and implementation
shape.

It does not mandate one optimal authoring path for every agent, worker or
runtime. Agentic coders may sometimes move faster by deriving
implementation and proof in the same work pass; that is acceptable only
when `co_evolution_admissible(B)` holds under proportional design
sequencing (§5) and the boundary reaches decision completeness before any
design-method closure claim (P0, P2).

One pillar of specification-driven development is bounded intermediate
traversal. Specification gives the global WHAT; every intermediate
traversal should have a finite, inspectable unit for reasoning,
implementation, evaluation, proof and later refactor. A module boundary is
one realisation-level tool for creating that unit; it is not the only
possible bounded traversal. Without bounded units, reviewers and agents
traverse too much context at once, and correctness depends on memory
rather than on preserved structure (P0; ACTIVATION §1 Execution unit).

The profile does not replace constitutional authority (SPEC_METHOD) and
does not replace the graph-native law of the graph-execution profile
(PROFILES §2). It governs how the Ontology, architecture and realisation
modules should be derived once the project has decided the outcomes and
capabilities it is building. A product decision that functionality is
required does not decide how many entities, functions, public operations,
carriers or modules should exist (P2, P6). For a product governed by the
graph-execution profile, this profile does not authorise replacing a graph
function, edge traversal or graph module with deterministic implementation
modules; it governs the deterministic realisation shape inside or beneath
those carriers (P6, §2).

These rules apply to module boundaries, schema and carrier families,
entity and record design, and interface contracts. They are not limited to
one programming language or one runtime binding (P1).

### Position

The preferred realisation shape is functionally biased (P1, P6;
rc.2 #2-position). That means semantic meaning should live in typed carriers and
explicit transforms; imperative coordination should be subordinate to
admitted truth; side effects should be isolated to explicit boundary
modules; and mutable shared state should be minimised and justified. The
profile does not require a functional programming language; it does
require a functional design discipline. A Python, Scala, TypeScript,
Kotlin or Java implementation may each satisfy it if it keeps semantic law
in explicit carriers and transforms rather than hidden orchestration.

### Core rule

Every performed evaluation returns one value of the core result algebra,
directly or as a refined value mapped into it (P5):

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `satisfied` | the declared predicate holds on the exact basis |
| `falsified` | a declared counterexample defeats it |
| `indeterminate` | the available admissible evidence cannot decide it |
| `out_of_frame` | the evaluation requires an undeclared material relation or capability |
| `invalid_basis` | the subject or basis cannot support the evaluation |

This core is the only one. Results of constraints, judgments, frame
evaluations, stops, work steps and effects are stated in it or in a
refinement mapped into it, so that results from any members combine under
one rule ([Conjunction of results](#conjunction-of-results)). Purpose and
material relation: no combination can report success while a failure, an
undecided question, an unperformed evaluation or an uncertain effect
remains, and none of these can be mistaken for another (P5, P6).

Recording. A result records its core value together with the predicate
evaluated and the original domain outcome, which is the refined value
where a refinement produced it. A mapping into the core never owns domain
meaning: the member, profile or adopting Product that defines the refined
value keeps it, and a consumer that needs the domain distinction reads the
domain outcome, never the core value alone (P1, P6).

Standing. The standing of a result is what it establishes about its
predicate; it is distinct from the standing of a commitment (§1). Only
`satisfied` establishes the predicate. `falsified` establishes that the
predicate fails and names the counterexample. `indeterminate`,
`out_of_frame` and `invalid_basis` establish neither, and each names what
would decide: the evidence, the missing relation or capability with its
owner where the subject gives one, or the basis repair. By support for the
predicate, `satisfied` stands above each other value, and the other four
are not ordered among themselves.

No refinement or mapping raises a result's standing (P5, P6):

- a falsified or failed result never maps to a satisfied or successful one;
- a result that admissible evidence cannot decide never maps to
  `satisfied`;
- an evaluation that was not performed stays distinct from one whose
  evidence cannot decide: it has no
  [closed result](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse), and it is never mapped
  to `indeterminate` or to any other core value;
- an effect whose completion is unknown never maps to no effect or to
  completed.

Not performed. An evaluation that is required or planned and was not
performed has no closed result; an actor cannot report an evaluation it
did not perform (P6). Nothing is coerced to success: a failed,
indeterminate, out-of-frame, out-of-scope or invalid-basis result follows
the declared result algebra and returns its own value under it, never
`satisfied`, and a missing result, being no result, enters every
conjunction over it as a gap: a planned assessment without a closed result
where an assessment was planned, and uncovered coverage where none was.
This
conserves
[RF-012](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/REFERENCE_FRAME_METHOD.md#rf-012-closed-results),
whose five values the table restates unchanged, and
[AC-007](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-007-constraint-and-refusal),
whose rule that a failed, missing, indeterminate, out-of-scope or
invalid-basis result follows the declared algebra rather than being
coerced to success is the sentence before; both are restated here once.
[REFERENCE_FRAME §3](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-012-closed-results) states
RF-012 as a law over frames and
[AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §4](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-007-constraint-and-refusal)
states AC-007 as a law over constraints; each uses this core and neither
defines it again.

Refinements. A member, profile or adopting Product that needs finer
outcomes defines a refinement. The refinement names the question it
answers and the predicate its mapping is for, and maps every refined value
to exactly one core value. No outcome exists outside the core; a
refinement adds no core value and keeps the pressure of `indeterminate`,
`out_of_frame` and `invalid_basis` explicit. Where a refined value would
map to one of two core values according to its cause, the cause is part of
the refined value and each resulting value maps once (P5, P1). A further
refinement, by a member, profile, project or adopting Product, may split a
refined value by cause. The parent-value rule governs every such split:
each child value names its parent value and its cause and keeps its
parent's core value; a child that needs a different core value needs a
different parent value, which only the owner of the parent declares; and
no child takes `satisfied` from a parent that is not `satisfied`. No
further refinement raises a result's standing (P5, P6, P1). Purpose and
material relation: a consumer that reads a parent value reads the same
core value from each of its children, so a split by cause adds a domain
distinction and never changes what the parent establishes (P5, P6). The
refinements for admission, activation and steps are
[ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition); each other
member, profile and adopting Product states its mapping where it defines
its values.

Availability, assessment and acceptance are separate results, each with its
own predicate: that a step produced a candidate; that the candidate meets
its declared criteria; and that the
[decision owner](ACTIVATION.md#roles-and-delegation) accepts it at its
boundary. A step having produced a candidate never maps to the candidate's
fitness or acceptance, and acceptance is never inferred from a successful
step (P6; [ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition),
[EVALUATION §4](EVALUATION.md#4-review-results) and
[§5](EVALUATION.md#5-acceptance)).

Out of frame or indeterminate. The boundary between these values is drawn
on what the activated frame declares and on what the step did with it (P5,
finite capacity and graceful total handling; the material relation drawn
is the three-way out_of_frame boundary: capability not declared, capability
declared and exercised, capability declared and not exercised; rc.2 RF
#rf-012-closed-results). Three cases; the first two name core values, and
the third names none:

- `out_of_frame` when the claim requires a material relation or an
  evaluator capability that the activated frame does not declare. The
  result names the missing relation or capability, its owner where the
  subject gives one, and the reconfiguration pressure it creates
  ([ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement); rc.2 RF
  #reconfigure-when-necessary). A term the claim depends on and the frame
  leaves undefined is an undeclared material relation: its meaning can
  alter the result and it enters through no declared input (rc.2 RF
  #material-relation, RF-003; P1). Whether the step exercised anything is
  irrelevant to this value; the ground is the missing declaration.
- `indeterminate` when the available admissible evidence cannot decide the
  claim (rc.2 RF-012). The result names the evidence that would decide, as
  its residual uncertainty (rc.2 RF #return-a-closed-result). Where the
  claim also depends on an undeclared relation or capability,
  `out_of_frame` and `indeterminate` each have a lawful ground; the result
  names the value it returns and that ground, and this boundary excludes
  neither (P5).
- no value of its own when the step did not exercise a declared capability
  the evaluation requires. A result is returned wherever a sufficient
  evaluation or an applicable judgment exists without that capability,
  identifying its evidence, verdict and residual uncertainty like any
  closed result (rc.2 RF #rf-012-closed-results, #return-a-closed-result):
  a counterexample found by what was exercised, as when source inspection
  falsifies A in a claim of A and B, returns `falsified`, and common
  agreement cannot discard it (rc.2 RF #result-conjunction). Where none
  exists because the capability was not exercised, the evaluation was not
  performed and has no result: the step's stop state carries it,
  `incomplete` under
  [construction availability](ACTIVATION.md#construction-availability), and
  its work state ([ACTIVATION §5](ACTIVATION.md#5-work-state-and-restart))
  carries the unexercised capability as a residual (P6). In either case
  the unexercised part, B above, has no result: in every conjunction over
  it, it is a planned assessment without a closed result, and the known
  failure A survives with it ([Conjunction of results](#conjunction-of-results)).

Who may adopt this profile is stated once in
[PRODUCT_DEFINITION §7](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#7-collective-reference-frame-basis):
inclusion in the selected method cut makes the profile available, and only
Product authority adopts it. This profile adds no adopter. The adopting
Product's authority may record its adoption by citing the profile in ADRs
or design surfaces; naming it in the project's agent entry surface (such
as `AGENTS.md`) as the preferred realisation discipline; using it as
review criteria for implementation-migration tickets; and classifying
implementation modules by the taxonomy of §9 (P2, P6;
rc.2 #15-adoption-guidance).

When the profile is adopted, the project applies it consistently across the
named boundary: Ontology and architecture derivation; design modules;
runtime or execution kernels; prompt assembly and reporting paths;
constructors and materialisers; and projection and query surfaces. For
migrations involving carrier closure, schema closure or governance
boundaries, projects should make the boundary closure evaluators (§3)
explicit in the governing ADR or ticket rather than leaving them implicit
(P6).

Every new or materially changed adopted semantic boundary declares or
cites its accepted Ontology before claiming design-method completion. The
Ontology evidence includes entity lifecycle, authority, function
derivation, whole-family Prime, each accepted atom's admitted domain,
atom-to-realisation projection mappings and projection traceability, at
the granularity applicable to the material change (P6, P2). When the
material change includes schema or typed carrier work, the project derives
and reconciles the IACS from that Ontology before claiming design-method
completion. When the new or materially changed boundary is derived from an
existing realisation, the project also publishes the reference-to-target
derivation asset and the Ontology-derived three-view design asset before
claiming design-method completion for the changed boundary. When the new or
materially changed boundary has active implementation, the project also
publishes a module-derived unit test lane (ASSURANCE §15) before claiming
closure for that change (P6).

Partial adoption is allowed, but the adopted boundary and adopted rule
family should be named explicitly. Partial adoption may narrow scope; it is
not used to claim design-method completion while skipping the evidence
needed to audit, refactor or reconstruct the realised boundary (P6, P2).

Tier 3. Owns the boundary between the core and the profiles, the
declared-binding rule and the import rule that every profile applies
(§1), and indexes the profiles (§2 to §6). A profile is a domain or
operational specialisation of the method; the members of tiers 1 and 2
are the core.

## 1. The boundary

The core names no runtime, no carrier and no executor. Terms owned outside
the core, by a profile, a realisation or an rc.2 member, never enter tier
1 or 2 except in a disposition table: graph, edge, vector, ledger, event
log, worksite, HoG, Markov overlay, screen, entity cut, and the design
profile's IACS and Prime. The traversal record and the functor kinds F_D,
F_P and F_H are tier-1 calculus terms owned by AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §5, and
"module" is a generic term, as the predecessor's generic testing law uses
it; neither is restricted here. A profile may bind a core mechanism to one of these;
the binding is declared in the profile with its direction, preserved
meaning, narrowed scope and invalidation. In this member "binding" means
that declared binding of a core mechanism; a Product's adoption binding is
[PRODUCT_DEFINITION §7](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#7-collective-reference-frame-basis)'s,
and a carrier binding to a typed contract is [UX §7](UX.md#7-carrier-binding)'s;
the three are not interchanged. The declared-binding rule is new
(P0 boundary, P1); its shape follows ODD's specialisations of F_P and F_H,
which [ODD §5 Probabilistic compute](ODD.md#probabilistic-compute) owns in
the graph-native context and carries as their provenance; the
predecessor's section is rc.2
[ODD probabilistic compute](stdo://releases/v2.5.1-rc.2/standards/ODD_METHOD.md#probabilistic-compute).

Import rule. A profile imports the generic families of tiers 1 and 2 that
its rules rest on, and owns only its own bindings: the terms and choices
it adds for its domain or operation, among them the declared bindings
above (P1, P6). It imports each concept it uses from a member of tiers 1
and 2 under
[FOUNDATIONS §2 Imports between members](FOUNDATIONS.md#imports-between-members),
which states what an import is, and restates none of that member's rules.
Its family table, in the format of
[FOUNDATIONS §3 Foundation to law](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundation-to-law),
names each imported family by its ID and the section that holds its table,
in the premise column; the profile's rules rest on that family's
consequences, with the standing FOUNDATIONS §3 gives them, and the
family's rules and choices keep their owners. A profile that refines
another profile declares the refinement in its lead; the refined profile
keeps its rules, and the refining profile owns only what it adds (P1, P6).
The import rule is new in this corpus. Purpose and material relation:
each profile table cites the families it rests on without restating them,
so no generic rule gains a second owner in a profile and no choice a
profile adds is presented as following from the foundations (P6, P1).

A worked application, a hello world or a data mapper is an external test
subject; its particulars cannot become generic method functionality by
precedent.

## 2. Graph execution

Graph execution is two tier-3 members, indexed here; each restates its
predecessor in full in its own text and declares its bindings under §1
(P0 boundary, P1):

| Member | Receives | Binds or adds |
|---|---|---|
| [ODD](ODD.md) | rc.2 ODD_METHOD, all 48 rows | the bounded step of FOUNDATIONS P0 to one vector or edge traversal and the graph-native F_P, F_D and F_H shorthands, with F_P and F_H as declared specialisations of SPEC_METHOD §5 ([§5 Probabilistic compute](ODD.md#probabilistic-compute)); the refinement of ACTIVATION §4 to graph functions, with the cumulative environment law of §11.8 declared as its specialised contract for carrying earlier outputs ([§5 Graph functions](ODD.md#graph-functions), [§11.8](ODD.md#118-cumulative-environment-law-is-mandatory)) |
| [TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE](TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE.md) | rc.2 TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE_PROFILE, all 26 rows, 25 conserved and 1 proposed superseded, pending the product owner | an optional closed model-family signature over one exact `a_c` basis of AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS for immutable occurrence histories over a mutable subject, with OP-001 to OP-007 |

The ownership split of graph execution (runtime, product, service layers)
is [ODD §10](ODD.md#10-what-an-odd-product-is); the worker's internal
solution strategy stays outside the framework under
[ODD §5](ODD.md#probabilistic-compute). Where another member says that
this section keeps the ODD binding, the binding is the one ODD states and
this section indexes (P0, P1).

## 3. Software design

[DESIGN_MODULE](DESIGN_MODULE.md) is the software-design profile. It
imports the core and binds: ontology-first derivation of operation
identities from discovered functionality through logical completeness,
Prime contraction, the irreducible architectural carrier set and its
projections; proportional design sequencing with the decision-complete
design gate; bounded frame conservation; native constructability;
capability and foundation selection; transformation admission
completeness; invariant reconstruction sufficiency; computational
realisation projection; the module taxonomy and realisation rules; and
the design review questions and checklist. Its design-to-module evidence
route, module-derived unit tests and module lifecycle confirmation are
ASSURANCE §14 to §16, and its core rule and non-goals SPEC_METHOD §2
Realisation shape. The per-boundary cost of the derivation chain is
decided there (DESIGN_MODULE §5 Proportional design sequencing, §7 Gate
and retrospective work) (P2, P0).

## 4. UX

[UX](UX.md) is the UX profile. It refines DESIGN_MODULE for modules that
realise a UX surface, imports the core, and binds: the Elm process model
with typed State, Msg, Update, View, Cmd and Sub; the boundary between UX
messages and admitted product carriers; the state transition law; the
effect membrane; binding to AssetSurface or an equivalent typed contract;
view continuation and the Msg-replay proof; view shape; type sharing with
runtime validation at untrusted seams; the accessibility minimum;
realisation discretion; adoption with the scaffold and exemption law and
UX sprint compliance escrow; the failure patterns and review questions;
and its refinements of the core result algebra, each value mapped to one
core value (UX §15). Its binding of TICKETS §3's generalised escrow terms
is declared in its lead (P6, P2).

## 5. World model

[WORLD_MODEL](WORLD_MODEL.md) is the world-model profile. It imports the
core and binds: the imported product-lineage concepts and the Builder
Project specialisation; the Markov-object construct at candidate status
with its effective blanket, working refinements, epistemic status and
promotion gate; the core claims and units; entity recovery and the entity
cut as the published identity-bearing unit, with its admissibility,
discrimination and publication law; the attribute ledger; the
representation, materialisation and publication laws; Markov-object
overlay construction; saturation; composition of local artifacts;
projection; the control and data planes; the proof law and
world-model-driven development; and its refinements of the core result
algebra, each value mapped to one core value (WORLD_MODEL §14). Its
binding of FOUNDATIONS §2 Object
and P3's boundary claim to the entity cut is declared in its lead.
Nothing in the core depends on the construct being established (P3, P6).

## 6. Engagement baseline

[EXECUTIVE_BASELINE](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md) is the optional
engagement-baseline profile. It imports the core and describes the
executive configuration, one configuration in the sense of
[ACTIVATION §1 Configuration](ACTIVATION.md#configuration), with three
engagement frames (Executive, Worker, Reviewer) and a catalogue of
specialist frames, mapped onto the law of tiers 1 and 2. Its frame names
bind the responsibilities that configuration allocates under
[ACTIVATION §1 Roles and delegation](ACTIVATION.md#roles-and-delegation),
not roles imported by spelling, as its lead declares (P1, P6).

## 7. Source dispositions

Each cell names where the rows of one rc.2 member receive their
dispositions. Every row's disposition is one of the four values of
[RELEASE §9](RELEASE.md#9-successor-baseline-conservation-stdo-up-015); a
row with none is unresolved, which blocks qualification of the claim it
affects.

| rc.2 member | Disposition |
|---|---|
| ODD_METHOD | conserved in full in ODD (all 48 rows; its §21), indexed in §2; the generic parts (bounded unit, refinement, loop structure) are generalised into ACTIVATION; the declared-binding rule of §1 is new |
| TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE_PROFILE | 25 rows conserved and 1 proposed superseded, pending the product owner, disposed in TRAVERSAL_OCCURRENCE, Source dispositions; indexed in §2 |
| baseline runtime bindings | disposed row by row in EXECUTIVE_BASELINE, with STDO_REFERENCE_FRAME_BASELINE; §6 is its index entry |

| UX_METHOD | disposed row by row in UX; §4 is its index entry. The first-pass description of UX by reader and task obligations, operational projection and screen-level acceptance was candidate text with no source in UX_METHOD, so it is no predecessor claim; it is withdrawn |
| WORLD_MODEL_METHOD | disposed row by row in WORLD_MODEL; §5 is its index entry; the generic identity and boundary law stays FOUNDATIONS §2 and P3 and IDENTITY, and the entity-cut law is WORLD_MODEL §9, bound to P3 by WORLD_MODEL's declared binding |
